explanation: Cache memory is a smaller, faster memory that sits between the CPU and main memory to speed up data access.  Direct-mapped caches are a type of cache organization where each memory address maps to exactly one location in the cache. This simplifies cache implementation but can lead to performance issues if multiple frequently accessed memory blocks map to the same cache location (cache collisions). Understanding cache behavior is crucial for optimizing program performance.
